title: Embodied impression capture — hiring loop notes (latent cues)
body:
Context: quick capture after the onsite loop for candidate N.B. (SWE, runtime infra). I wanted to record the small, non-technical signals that are hard to fit into a formal scorecard but matter when imagining them on the team. Use this as background color for the formal debrief.

High-level first impression (3-line):
- Calm, deliberately paced answers; not theatrical but confident.
- Repeatedly returned to previous points to check alignment (good for cross-team syncs).
- Slightly guarded on architecture tradeoffs — expresses preferences strongly, wants evidence.

Short timeline (by segment, approximate):
- 09:05 intro chat w/ recruiter (5m): friendly, clear logistics questions. Not a lot of small talk.
- 09:15 system design half-hour: drew a dataflow sketch rapidly, asked clarifying Qs about SLOs before diving in. Brought up KV cache eviction as an initial concern (shows infra pattern awareness).
- 09:50 deep dive w/ runtime lead (45m): asked about kernel selection heuristics and quantization tradeoffs; when pushed, gave a concise tradeoff matrix instead of long monologue.
- 10:40 culture / collaboration loop (30m): candid about past team friction; framed failures as learning loops.

Non-verbal / tonal cues I noticed:
- Breath control: patient, rarely filled silence. When thinking, paused long and used clarifying questions rather than guessing.
- Hands: used tabletop gestures when drawing architecture; tends to mimic interviewer gestures (rapport signal).
- Micro-expressions: small smile when interviewer said "we ship nightly" — seems to value shipping cadence.

Concrete behavioral signals (why this matters):
- Prefers explicit metrics. Asked repeatedly for latency/cost SLO numbers before proposing caching. Likely to be good at disciplined optimization work (Optimize product fit).
- Defensive shorthand: when pressed on a past failure, immediately quantified impact (numbers first) and then described fix; suggests data-driven blamelessness.
- Cross-functional sensitivity: asked about product constraints and customer pain rather than only technical purity. Good for product-facing infra roles.

Risks / open questions to flag for debrief:
- May default to conservative designs in ambiguity — could slow prototypes. Confirm appetite for tradeoff-driven shipping speed.
- Less depth on distributed systems debugging at 3am: when asked about a cascading KV cache failure, they leaned on hypotheticals rather than concrete postmortem steps. Need to probe with a postmortem case study if we care.

Quick informal score (relative to other onsite candidates, 1-5):
- Technical breadth: "4"
- Deep kernel/quantization chops: "3"
- Systems debugging / incident triage: "3"
- Cross-team communication: "5"
- Shipping bias: "3"

Concrete candidate quotes to use in debrief (verbatim-ish):
- "Show me the SLOs and I'll show you the appropriate cache policy."
- "I don't like to commit to a single kernel until I see tail latency and memory pattern traces."
- "In the last outage, our telemetry lagged by 12 minutes; that drove most of our wrong decisions."

Suggested probe questions for follow-up (if we want to push):
- Walk me through a postmortem you wrote that changed runtime behavior (what was the decision, who owned it, what metric moved?).
- Give me a concrete list of commands/steps you'd run when a cluster's p99 jumps 3x during a release window.
- If you had to trade 10% throughput for 30% lower p99, what levers would you pull first on a GPU-based serving fleet?

Hiring-manager level recommendation (raw):
- Consider for strong cross-functional infra SWE role (prod-facing runtime engineer).
- Not a slam dunk for "deep inference kernel" specialist without extra verification.

Operational notes / next steps I took: 
- Posted short flags and this summary into #hiring-runtime with a pointer to HIRE-4321.
- Dropped a request for a 30m follow-up focused on incident postmortems (owner: Aisha).
- Suggested a simulated troubleshooting exercise as a take-home if we want to validate on-call muscle.

Meta notes to self:
- This doc is intentionally subjective — remove color in the formal scorecard.
- When we synthesize, call out which signals are reproducible (e.g., asked for SLOs) vs. ephemeral (e.g., small smile at shipping cadence).

Unresolved internal questions (put into debrief agenda):
- Does the hiring manager prefer prototypers who favor speed or engineers who lock down correctness first? (ask Alex G.)
- How important is deep quantization kernel experience vs. system-level incident ownership for this role?

Links / artifacts I referenced during interviews: 
- HIRE-4321 (loop schedule, panel list)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hiring-profiles/pull/98 (candidate materials we shared)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01XXXXXXX/p1700xxxxx

Bottom-line 1-sentence: candid, product-aware runtime engineer who tilts toward disciplined, metrics-led decisions; recommend an incident-focused follow-up before offering for roles that require deep kernel-level debugging at scale.

---
Notes timestamp: 2025-11-04 07:20 PST (just after debrief).
